newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies begin voting oil bill amendments.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies begin voting oil bill amendments.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies began voting on a series of amendments to a bill opening up the country's oil and gas sectors to private competition, an official said.
About 30 amendments to the bill, which was approved by the lower house last week, were due to be voted by the chamber, but most were expected to be defeated.

However, one amendment which has the backing of government-allied parties would give licensed distributors of petroleum derivatives and natural gas exclusive distribution rights for five years after approval of the bill.
Steelmakers, petrochemical and chemical companies and thermoelectric power plants would be allowed to sidestep the distributors and buy direct from refineries.

Another amendment would eliminate from the bill an article which requires the Brazilian state to retain control of publicly owned oil and gas giant Petrobras, allowing for a future privatization of the company.
Once the amendments have been voted, the bill advances to the Senate.
